course_description: This course provides students with a 20-day student-led placement experience in a foodservice setting. Students will apply theoretical knowledge of foodservice principles and systems to real-world contexts and complete a project aimed at making quality improvements to the foodservice system. Sudents will develop professional skills in communication, problem-solving, teamwork and reflective practice, while gaining insight into the role of the foodservice dietitian. This course consolidates learning from the theory component and prepares students for entry-level dietetic practice in foodservice environments.

course_aims: This course aims to develop advanced skills and practice in food service management relevant to dietetics professionals.

learning_outcomes.description: Apply foodservice management principles and a systems approach to assess, plan and evaluate processes or quality improvement opportunities within a foodservice.
Demonstrate project management skills by critically investigating foodservice practice problems using research, evidence and evaluation, and developing practical, feasible recommendations.
Demonstrate effective collaboration, teamwork and communication skills, with peers and interdisciplinary teams.
Demonstrate safe, ethical, professional and culturally responsive dietetic practice.
Proactively engage in feedback and reflective processes to identify areas for improvement and enhance professional practice performance.
